_comment: What the host did with a hook output, observed by emitting one and reading the verdict.
`hook: <Event> Failed` per firing, which is the whole signal: `Failed` is the host refusing
the output, and the other two are it taking the output. Each entry below is one probe --
one output shape and the verdict on it, per event it was emitted from.
Two kinds of probe. A key probe (`suppressOutput`) answers every event in one session with
the same output. A Stop probe (`systemMessage`, `block-once`) answers the first Stop only
and every other event with `{}`, so its only verdict is the one on Stop.
This is the externally-verified half of `codex-output-rules.json`. That table states what
this plugin must not emit; the entries here are the subset of it a run of the real binary
has actually confirmed. `codex-payload.test.mjs` cross-checks the two, so the contract
cannot drift away from the observation without a test saying so.
Only events that print a verdict in the probe session appear. `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`,
`SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` need a session shape the probe does not reach, and on
codex-cli 0.154.0 `codex exec` runs the `SessionEnd` hook without printing a verdict for it,
so they are absent rather than assumed -- see `README.md`.
